Problem Statement:
✨ Show a clear error on attempt to include router into itself

Previously discussed in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/11424 with the PR at https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/11425

Since I made modifications in the fork of the repo, the PR was automatically closed. This PR serves to add the circular reference check again. Discussed again in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/14251

The issue is that `APIRouter.include_router` allows a router to be included within itself, which can lead to circular references and potential infinite loops in some contexts. The goal is to add a check to prevent this and raise a clear error.

`FastAPI.include_router` simply delegates to `self.router.include_router`, so the fix should be implemented in `APIRouter.include_router`.

FILES: `fastapi/routing.py`
ROOT CAUSE: Missing check to prevent a router from including itself.
CHANGE: In `APIRouter.include_router`, add a check `if router is self: raise FastAPIError("You cannot include a router into itself")`.
TEST: A new test case in a file like `tests/test_include_router.py` (or similar) that attempts to include a router into itself and asserts a `FastAPIError` is raised.

Specifically, in `fastapi/routing.py`, the check should be added at the beginning of the `include_router` method:

```python
    def include_router(
        self,
        router: Annotated["APIRouter", Doc("The `APIRouter` to include.")],
        # ... other args ...
    ) -> None:
        if router is self:
            raise FastAPIError("You cannot include a router into itself")
        # ... rest of the method ...
```
